package_info.why_malicious: This article does not describe a specific malicious package, but rather outlines operational risk factors in open-source software supply chains that can lead to security issues. These risks are not always captured by CVEs and include end-of-life status, outdated versions, infrequent updates, and inactive project communities. Such conditions can make software vulnerable to exploitation or unpatched security flaws.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Component is marked as End-of-Life or has not received updates for over 40 months.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At project maintenance time, the component is no longer maintained or updated, meaning discovered vulnerabilities will not be patched, leading to persistent risk.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unmaintained or end-of-life components are not monitored for vulnerabilities and will not receive security patches.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal open-source components are actively maintained and patched; end-of-life components are abandoned and pose a risk.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Archival of legacy software for historical purposes, not for production use.
key_indicators: No updates or releases for extended periods

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Component version is more than 40 months old or lags 6+ releases behind the latest.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At project maintenance time, the component is significantly outdated, increasing the likelihood of unpatched vulnerabilities and incompatibility with modern security practices.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Old versions are less likely to have recent security fixes and may depend on other outdated, vulnerable components.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal practice is to use up-to-date versions; using very old versions increases risk.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legacy systems with strict compatibility requirements.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Component has fewer than 2 releases per year, fewer than 100 commits per year, or fewer than 5 unique contributors per year.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At project maintenance time, the component shows low activity, indicating a lack of community engagement and reduced oversight, which can allow vulnerabilities to persist unnoticed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Low activity suggests the project is not actively maintained, making it less likely that vulnerabilities will be found and fixed.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Healthy open-source projects have regular releases, frequent commits, and multiple contributors.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Small, niche projects with limited scope.

attack_chain.action: Component is selected for use despite being end-of-life, outdated, or inactive.
attack_chain.leads_to: Increased risk of unpatched vulnerabilities and potential exploitation.

attack_chain.action: Vulnerabilities in the component remain unpatched due to lack of maintenance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers exploit known or unknown vulnerabilities in production environments.

behavioral_signatures: Use of end-of-life or unmaintained components
Components lagging 6 or more releases behind the latest
Projects with fewer than 2 releases, 100 commits, or 5 contributors per year
file_indicators: SBOM entries with old version numbers
Lack of recent commit or release metadata in repository
network_indicators: N/A (operational risk, not runtime network behavior)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Regularly scan your SBOM and dependency list for components that are end-of-life, have not been updated in over 40 months, lag 6+ releases behind, or show low project activity (few releases, commits, or contributors per year). Use automated tools like JFrog Xray to enforce policy rules and flag risky components for review or replacement.
